chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi said: Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi said on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Qasim that I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) saying:
He who compares Allah with His creation is an infidel, and he who limits Him spatially is an unbeliever. And he who attributes to Him what is forbidden is a liar.
Only they forge the lie who do not believe in Allah’s communications, and these are the liars.
ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that make one an infidel, unbeliever, or liar regarding the description of God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida delineates the triad of theological errors—shirk, kufr, and kadhib—corresponding to comparison, spatiality, and attributes of imperfection, respectively, establishing a precise framework for Shia Tawhid. By linking these specific negations to the verse from Surah Yunus, the Imam emphasizes that attributing false qualities to God is not merely an error but a fundamental lie against divine revelation. This narration serves as a cornerstone for the school of Akhbari and Usuli scholars in distinguishing between essential divine attributes and accidental limitations.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 25. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: `Ali ibn alHusayn al-Sa`dabadi said: Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Barqi said on the authority of dawud ibn al-Qasim that I heard `Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) that
“He who compares Allah with His creation is an infidel and he who limits Him spatially is an unbeliever. And he who attributes to Him what is forbidden is a liar.”
Then he (AS) recited this verse: Only they forge the lie who do not believe in Allah’s communications, and these are the liars.
